summary: The guest is one host's actual ex-partner, and the audience treats it as the most excruciating and most enjoyable episode of the series. The running joke — host one is villager one, host two is villager two, the viewer is villager three — captures the frame precisely: everyone including the audience is a bystander to two people who clearly still feel something. Comments track his avoidance of eye contact, the fact that he still picks her when given a choice, and that they drank from the same glass. The clearest demand to come out of it is structural: do this again with the other two hosts' exes, with commenters organising upvotes behind the request. Viewers also ask for the guest to be carried across to the channel's other series, and the guest himself replies in the thread.

audience_signals: Booking a host's real ex-partner is the strongest chemistry device the series has found, and the audience immediately asks for it to be repeated with the other two — a ready-made format extension
The 'villager number three' meme shows the audience positions itself alongside the non-participating hosts as co-spectators, which is a participatory frame worth writing into the format
Guests replying in the comments lifts the whole thread and should be encouraged as part of the booking arrangement
Cross-series funnelling is requested by the audience, not imposed — moving a popular guest between programmes is welcomed rather than resented
All ten of this series' top episodes turn on real or suspected romance; the format's value is access to genuine relationships, not the questions themselves
